summary: Network-device registration updates dev->reg_state while a sysfs show callback reads it through dev_isalive without dev_base_lock coverage.

call_chain.evidence: KCSAN write stack reports register_netdevice and merged.ll defines it.
type_show is generated through the netdev_show helper path.
Inline helper reads dev->reg_state for sysfs visibility.

interleaving: register_netdevice publishes a net_device and writes dev->reg_state.
A sysfs read of the type attribute concurrently calls type_show and dev_isalive on the same net_device.
The fix moves reg_state transitions under dev_base_lock so the sysfs-side alive check has matching protection.

ground_truth_access.required_ordering: reg_state transitions and dev_isalive readers must be synchronized by RTNL or dev_base_lock.

vulnerability_surface.why_relevant: reg_state is the shared device lifecycle state that sysfs uses to decide whether an attribute can be reported while registration changes the state.

aliases.name: dev->reg_state
aliases.evidence: register_netdevice writes the lifecycle state after netdev_register_kobject().

aliases.name: ndev->reg_state
aliases.evidence: netdev_show converts the device object to struct net_device and calls dev_isalive.

aliases.name: dev->reg_state
aliases.evidence: dev_isalive reads the state flag directly.

thread_a.evidence: The registration entry receives the net_device pointer and writes its state.

thread_b.evidence: type_show/netdev_show derive the net_device from the sysfs device before dev_isalive.

allocated_by: network driver allocates struct net_device before registration
published_by: register_netdevice and netdev_register_kobject publish the device and sysfs attributes
invalidated_by: unregister_netdevice_many and netdev_run_todo transition reg_state during teardown

coverage.analysis_conclusion: The required files define the writer, the sysfs show callback, and the reg_state reader; external stack frames establish one observed caller but are not part of the patched access pair.

patch_hunks: cc26c2661fef moves reg_state updates under dev_base_lock and documents dev_isalive caller locking.
indirect_edges: type_show is a netdevice sysfs show callback reached through device attribute dispatch.
KCSAN write stack shows register_netdevice reached through a notifier-driven lapbeth path.
entry_discovery_log: merged.ll defines register_netdevice, type_show, and dev_isalive.
